semantics.catering_provided: Does the venue provide catering (in-house catering available). yes = the venue states it provides catering in-house; no = the venue's own published text states that food is renter-supplied or must come from an outside caterer, with the arrangement quoted in conditions; unknown = the checked pages do not state who supplies the food. Silence is never no.
semantics.delivery_allowed: Does the venue allow food delivery (Uber Eats, DoorDash, outside food). yes = outside food is permitted or contemplated on site; no = outside food is explicitly prohibited; unknown = the page does not address it.
semantics.beer_allowed: Does the venue allow beer / alcohol. yes = alcohol may be served (with any stated conditions); no = alcohol is prohibited; unknown = the page does not address it.

notes: A page that is silent on a fact is recorded unknown with a verification_question, never no.

source_locator markers: plain text is a verbatim quote from source_url; [silent] means the cited pages were read and say nothing; [not stated] means the page discusses the topic but never states the answer.
conditions carry every caveat (surcharges, certifications, room restrictions) and name the page when a quoted sentence lives somewhere other than source_url.
Each quote was matched against the page text fetched on 2026-11-22 (whitespace-normalised); the Four One Nine quotes come from the PDF text layer.
Per-field confidence: high = the page directly supports the recorded value (including a documented silence); medium = a related rule or a third-party/archived source.
Third-party listing only for Common Space (Peerspace, read from the 2026-04-06 archive snapshot because the live page was Cloudflare-blocked).

Fact keys are catering_provided / delivery_allowed / beer_allowed, matching MARK_FIELDS in plan-event/scripts/city_rank.py. The store's pre-existing scored field fields.catering (the catering_policy enum) is never written by this bundle.
Revision 2: Brava Lobby, Brava Studio, RWOH and Four One Nine moved from catering no to unknown because their pages never state who supplies the food; the quoted sentences stay in conditions.
The card's verify_command line 1 reads v['catering']; that key was renamed to catering_provided under review, so the equivalent assertion is sorted({v['catering_provided']['value'] ...}).
